title: Enterprise Onboarding + Health, QBR & Escalation Playbook (Onboard -> Operate -> Escalate)
author: Morgan Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates the standard enterprise onboarding checklist, integration guidance, health-check and QBR materials, an operational escalation matrix, and a curated list of known issues and workarounds for Redwood Inference customers. The goal is to provide a single reference for CSMs, SEs, SREs, and Support engineers during the first 90 days of a customer engagement and for ongoing quarterly reviews.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs)
- Support Engineers
- SRE/Platform contacts
- Enterprise customers' integration teams

Scope:
Covers: initial technical onboarding, integration checklist, acceptance criteria, daily/weekly health checks, QBR content and cadence, escalation routing for Sev1/2 incidents, and common issues + mitigations. Does not replace product docs or infra runbooks; links to those sections are included in Related Pages.

Owners & Contacts:
- Playbook owner: Morgan Chen (customer-success)
- Support escalation owner: Diego Martinez (eng-sre)
- Dedicated account SE: assigned per contract (see account metadata)
- Pager duty: Redwood Support (primary) - support@redwood.ai / +1-888-555-0102

Onboarding checklist (90-day, numbered):
1. Kickoff (Day 0-3)
   1.1 Schedule technical kickoff with CSM, SE, customer infra lead, and SRE representative.
   1.2 Share onboarding timeline, success criteria, and communication channels (Slack channel + ticketing queue).
2. Account & Access (Day 0-7)
   2.1 Verify customer has correct org & project created in Redwood Console.
   2.2 Provision API keys and, if applicable, set up dedicated capacity or private deployment credentials.
   2.3 Confirm KMS/HSM integration (if required) and audit logging configuration.
3. Integration (Day 3-21)
   3.1 Validate the following with the customer: sample prompt flows, expected QPS, peak concurrency, average prompt length and max sequence length.
   3.2 Run a smoke test using the SDK and REST API using the customer API key. Example curl:
       curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"Hello"}'
   3.3 Confirm network & egress rules for private deployments (IP allowlist or VPC peering).
4. Performance & Cost Tuning (Day 7-30)
   4.1 Enable prefix caching and recommended batching settings for the workload.
   4.2 Apply quantization profile recommendations from eng-applied-ml when using large models.
   4.3 Run perf benchmark: 95th percentile latency target <= agreed SLO. Document results.
5. Acceptance & Go-Live (Day 21-60)
   5.1 Validate acceptance criteria: functional correctness, latency SLOs, cost baseline, and security checklist items.
   5.2 Sign-off by customer PO and CSM.

Integration guide (technical highlights):
- Required information to collect from the customer:
  - Expected QPS and p50/p95 latency targets
  - Typical prompt length distribution (tokens) and maximum sequence length
  - Allowed model catalog (if restricting models for compliance)
  - Network topology (VPC, NAT, proxies) and firewall rules
- Standard integration steps:
  - Create API key with least-privilege scope for integration tests.
  - Run sample SDK tests (Node/Python/Go) and verify token usage metrics appear in Console usage dashboard within 10 minutes.
  - If using streaming or tool-calling features, validate SSE/WebSocket connectivity and callback URLs for tool responses.
- Security checklist (table):
  | Item | Requirement | Verification | Owner |
  |------|-------------|--------------|-------|
  | API key rotation | Rotate every 90 days (recommended) | Confirm rotation schedule in account settings | Customer/SE |
  | KMS integration | Customer-managed keys for Private deployment | Demo encryption-at-rest & audit logs | SE/Security |
  | Audit logging | Retain for 180 days (enterprise plan) | Access sample logs from Console | Customer/SRE |

Health checks (daily/weekly):
- Daily (automated):
  - Token usage by route (alert if > 30% above baseline)
  - Error rate by model (5xx and 4xx) — alert on > 1% of requests in 5m window
  - Queue length / request latency (p95) per serving pool
- Weekly (CSM+SE review):
  - Cost-per-inference trend and top 3 cost drivers
  - Accuracy / quality regression checks on canonical prompt set (run eval harness)
  - Capacity headroom and upcoming change requests

QBR content & cadence (quarterly):
- QBR owners: CSM (facilitator), SE (technical lead), Finance (billing summary)
- Standard QBR deck sections:
  1. Executive summary: adoption, topline usage, and key wins
  2. Reliability & performance: SLO attainment, incidents since last QBR, MTTR trends
  3. Cost & unit economics: cost per 1k tokens, optimization recommendations (batching/quantization)
  4. Quality & accuracy: evaluation results on canonical prompts, regression alerts, examples
  5. Roadmap & requests: upcoming feature rollouts, model upgrades, capacity planning
  6. Action items and owners
- Deliverables before QBR: updated usage deck, three representative prompts, and any failing evals with remediation plans.

Escalation matrix & procedures (operational playbook):
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev1 (P0) — Production outage or total loss of inference for customer, > 50% of requests failing, critical business impact.
  - Sev2 (P1) — Major feature degraded (significant latency increase >3x p95 baseline or >10% errors), partial loss of functionality.
  - Sev3 (P2) — Non-critical bug impacting a subset of customers or features with a known workaround.
  - Sev4 (P3) — General questions, enhancement requests, or low-priority issues.
- Response & escalation timelines:
  | Severity | Initial response | Target response SLA | Escalation step after | Primary owner |
  |---------:|----------------:|--------------------:|---------------------:|--------------:|
  | Sev1     | 15 minutes      | 1 hour              | 30 minutes           | Eng-SRE on-call |
  | Sev2     | 30 minutes      | 4 hours             | 8 hours              | Support lead / SE |
  | Sev3     | 2 hours         | 24 hours            | 3 business days      | Support queue owner |
  | Sev4     | 1 business day  | 7 business days      | N/A                  | CSM / Product |
- Escalation steps (numbered):
  1. Triage in support ticket with full reproduction steps and logs attached.
  2. If Sev1/2, create an incident channel (Slack) and notify on-call SRE via PagerDuty.
  3. Designate incident commander (IC) — typically Eng-SRE lead on duty.
  4. IC coordinates immediate mitigations: traffic routing to fallback model, capacity rebalancing, temporary throttling.
  5. Post-incident: run a postmortem within 72 hours (owner: Eng-SRE) and capture action items.

Known issues & workarounds (curated at time of publication):
- Table (text):
  | Issue ID | Symptom | Typical cause | Workaround | Owner |
  |---------:|---------|---------------|-----------|-------|
  | KI-2026-017 | Streaming responses stall after token 1024 for some Node SDK clients | SDK buffering + proxy timeout | Upgrade client SDK to 1.4.2+, set keepalive on proxy to 120s. Temporary: use short-lived chunked responses. | Eng-DevEx |
  | KI-2026-021 | Elevated 5xx errors during autoscale events | Instance warmup race condition | Apply canary routing or increase buffer pool; contact Eng-SRE to expand dedicated pool temporarily. | Eng-SRE |
  | KI-2026-030 | Token accounting mismatch between Console and billing export (<1%) | Rounding/truncate behavior in export job | Use monthly reconciliation job script (link in related pages); escalate to Finance if discrepancy > $500 | Finance/Support |
- How to add a new Known Issue: submit issue doc to /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage and link to this playbook.

Support process & ticketing (practical steps):
1. Create a support ticket with reproduction, logs (request/response ids), timestamps, model and route.
2. Triage owner tags severity and assigns to queue.
3. For Sev1/2, open incident channel and notify SRE/SE. For Sev3/4, handle through normal SLA routing.
4. Communicate to customer at these cadences: initial ack within the response SLA, status updates every 30 minutes for Sev1, every 2 hours for Sev2, daily for Sev3.
5. Close ticket with root cause, remediation steps, and customer confirmation.

Runbooks & playbook links (quick references):
- perf playbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite
- incident response runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- billing reconciliation script: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing

Maintenance & review cadence:
- Playbook review: owner reviews quarterly and after major incidents.
- Known issues list: updated by Support weekly, triaged monthly with Eng-Platform.
- QBR deck template: updated by CSMs semi-annually.

Appendix: example acceptance criteria (text):
- Functional: example chat prompts produce expected structured output for 95% of golden prompt set.
- Performance: p95 latency <= agreed SLA (example: 250ms for short prompts, 1200ms for long prompts).
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and no more than one Sev2 in 90 days.
- Cost: month-over-month CPU/GPU spend growth <= 20% without corresponding usage growth.

Revision history:
- 2026-05-01: Created by Morgan Chen (initial draft).
- 2026-06-10: Reviewed and published; added known issues KI-2026-030 and updated escalation SLAs (reviewers: Priya Kapoor, Diego Martinez).

Contact & feedback:
If you find missing content or procedural gaps, please add a change request to the playbook by pinging the owner (Morgan Chen) or opening a pull request on the internal docs repo.
